changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names to standard format (Llama-3-8B, Llama-2-7B) and corrected dataset name (MathBench). The paper clearly addresses NLG tasks including code generation and mathematical reasoning.

Removed statistical measures (Gini, CV, Kurtosis) that were used for analyzing activation patterns but not for evaluating NLG outputs. Kept metrics used for evaluating generated outputs (Accuracy) and analyzing relationships between tasks (R-squared, Correlation Coefficient, MSE).
No LLM-as-judge evaluation was conducted in this paper. The LLMs mentioned are used as generation models, not as evaluators.
No human evaluation was conducted in this paper. All evaluations used automatic metrics.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on analyzing attention head activation patterns during supervised fine-tuning (SFT) rather than comprehensive NLG evaluation. The NLG evaluation is limited to accuracy metrics on specific tasks. The paper's main contribution is understanding the mechanisms of rapid generalization in SFT through attention pattern analysis.
